links.comparator_used: Radiographer interpretation alone (baseline read before seeing AI output), against a radiologist reference standard; standalone AI performance also reported
links.outcome: Fracture detection accuracy of radiographers on 2496 paired reads
links.effect: Accuracy 97.6% at baseline vs 98.0% with AI assistance (exact McNemar p = 0.0064); with AI, radiographers corrected 11 errors and introduced 1, a net gain of 10 cases. Subgroup gains were directionally consistent but not significant after correction.
links.tradeoff: Benefit was small. Radiographers changed their decision in only 11 of 729 discordant cases, and most negative interactions were correct AI recommendations not adopted. One new error was introduced. No or incomplete AI output was returned for 8.8% of examinations. Downstream clinical outcomes were not measured.
links.quote: Radiographers’ baseline accuracy was high (97.6%; specificity 99.0%) and improved modestly with AI assistance (98.0%; exact McNemar p = 0.0064).

design_hint: radiographer review of AI output with human-in-the-loop (with vs without AI assistance)
